dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Same thing?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Same thing.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You've been in here every day this week.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You're the closest thing to a kitchen I have right now.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: That's not good.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It's fine.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You want hot sauce on that?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: It's on the house. Don't tell anyone.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You never told me your name.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You never asked.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: I'm asking now.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It's —

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Good. I'm Carlos. This is my place. Has been for fourteen years.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: How's business?

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: It's a bodega in New York City. It is always business.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You need anything else or are you just here for the cat again?

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You know how long this block has been changing?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Since before I got here, I'm guessing.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Since before my father got here. Every five years it changes. The faces, the prices, the businesses. Only the building shapes stay.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Does it bother you?

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Some days. Some days I think — the neighbourhood is the people. Not the buildings. The people keep coming. That part doesn't change.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: You're staying, right? You're not one of those two-year people?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I don't know yet.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Honest answer. I respect it.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Hey. Come here.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: What's wrong?

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: Nothing's wrong. A lady came in yesterday — Mrs. Okafor, third floor of the blue building on 34th — she's moving to be near her daughter. Her apartment is up at the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: It's a one-bedroom. She's been there twelve years. Landlord is old school, hasn't raised the rent in three years.

dialogue.speaker: carlos
dialogue.text: I told her I might know someone.

choices.label: Ask Carlos to introduce you
Thank him but stay where you are

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: So. How long have you been at the company?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: About a year. Little over.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Honestly?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I wouldn't ask if I wanted the polished answer.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It's fine. The work is fine. I thought I'd feel more settled by now.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Nobody feels settled. We're just pretending harder each year. Welcome to your thirties.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That's bleak.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: It's realistic. Another round?

choices.label: Yes, another round
No, early morning

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Can I ask you something weird?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: The Henderson deck — the one I've been working on for three weeks — I need a second pair of eyes. Someone who'll actually tell me if something's off.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You're asking me?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: You're the only one here who doesn't have a political reason to lie to me.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That's a very specific thing to know about someone.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I pay attention.

choices.label: Look at it tonight and give real feedback
Look at it but keep feedback light
Decline — too much on your plate

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I didn't get it.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The promotion?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: They went with David. David who has been here two years less than me and whose main qualification appears to be that he plays golf.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, Priya.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Don't apologise. It's not your fault. I just needed to say it to someone who isn't going to immediately make it about office politics.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: What are you going to do?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I don't know yet. Something. I'm good at what I do. That has to count eventually.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Doesn't it?

choices.label: Tell her the truth — it should count, and sometimes it doesn't, and that's worth being angry about
Encourage her to stay and keep pushing
Suggest she start looking elsewhere

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I talked to Sarah.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: About?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: About you. For the role.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Priya — I didn't ask you to do that.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I know you didn't. That's why it'll land differently than if you had.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: You've been here, you've done the work. You helped me when you didn't have to. That's the kind of thing I remember. Apparently I'm not the only one.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: What did Sarah say?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: She said to make sure you apply properly this time. None of this 'I'll think about it' business.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Ah. You knocked.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It's midnight.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The music is very loud.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: It is Coltrane. You cannot listen to Coltrane quietly. This is known.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I have work tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Everyone in New York has work tomorrow. This does not stop Coltrane.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Could you maybe —

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: I will turn it down. Slightly. This is my compromise.

choices.label: Accept the compromise — slightly down is fine
Hold firm — actually quiet, please
Ask what he's listening to

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I am tired.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Work?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Work. The city. All of it.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: How long have you been here?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Few months.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Ah. Still in the hard part. It gets less hard.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: When?

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Different for everyone. For me it was the second winter. I stopped fighting it and started just... living in it.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That's either advice or a threat.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: With New York it is always both.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Saturday. Some people are coming. Friends. We eat, we listen to music, we argue about things that don't matter.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That sounds like a dinner party.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: I would never call it that. It is just people in a room. You should come.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I don't really know anyone you know.

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: Now you do. Bring something if you want. Don't bring something if you don't. Either is acceptable.

choices.label: Go, bring a bottle of wine
Go, bring nothing
Skip it — not feeling social

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: I have something for you.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Should I be concerned?

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: It is a key. To my apartment.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: ...Why?

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: I travel sometimes. Not often, but sometimes. When I do, the plants need water. The cat needs food. I need someone who will not steal my records.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You have a cat?

dialogue.speaker: dima
dialogue.text: He hides when there are people. You haven't seen him. He has seen you. He likes you. I trust his judgment.

choices.label: Take the key
Decline but offer to help when needed

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: Okay wait, wait — so you know how I've been working on the series?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The photo series. Yes.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: A gallery in Bushwick wants to see it. Not a definite yes, but a 'we're interested in seeing more.'

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Jordan, that's actually great.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: I know! I know it is. I just need to finish the last twelve photos and get them printed and —

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: How much does printing cost?

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: A completely reasonable amount that I currently do not have.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Of course.

choices.label: Celebrate first, figure out the money later
Celebrate and offer to help them think through the budget
Point out this has happened before

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: are you up

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Jordan it's 2am.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: okay so that's technically a yes

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: i got rejected from the grant. the big one.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: i really thought this was the one. i had a whole plan.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I know you did.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: does it ever get less — like. does it stop feeling like you're building something and someone just keeps knocking it over?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Sometimes it stops. Sometimes you just get better at building.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: that's either inspirational or very sad

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Yeah.

choices.label: Stay up and talk
Send a voice note and go back to sleep
Reply in the morning

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: It's happening. The show. It's actually happening.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: When?

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: Six weeks. The gallery confirmed. It's a group show but I have the whole east wall.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Jordan.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: I know. I know. Don't make me cry in this bar.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'm not doing anything.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: You're doing that face.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: What face?

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: The face that means you're actually happy for me. It's a good face. Stop it.

choices.label: Go to the opening
Help them promote it on social

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: So. I sold a piece.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: From the show?

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: From the show. A collector came in on the second day. She bought the big one — the one I almost didn't include because I thought it was too personal.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That's the best kind to sell.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: She paid twelve hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Jordan.

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: I know. And — here.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: What is this?

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: It's the two hundred I owe you. Plus forty. The forty is interest. I know you didn't ask for interest. I'm charging it anyway.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You don't have to —

dialogue.speaker: jordan
dialogue.text: I want to. You believed in me when I didn't have a very good track record of deserving it. That's worth forty dollars.
